attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post, endorsed.

semantics.note: From the context, the lab is Anthropic and the cause is the June White House decision. 'Will' makes it a firm forecast with no deadline and no stated size.

contract.note: The plain reading is an actual delay or interruption of Anthropic's deployments or research caused by the decision. That is a fair, ordinary reading of 'slow down', though a minimal one. The speaker set no length or size threshold, and the contract requires the effect to continue after publication.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own notice, dated June 30. It says both models stayed suspended after the June 12 directive until controls were lifted June 30. Fable returned July 1 and Mythos only to vetted US groups. The interruption continued after June 14.
June 12 notice from before the post. It sets the scope: only Fable 5 and Mythos 5 were suspended, and other models were unaffected.

reviews.rationale: The early-resolution rule is met. Anthropic's dated disclosure shows the directive kept its newest models suspended until June 30 or July 1, with Mythos access still limited after that. That is a deployment slowdown caused by the decision and lasting past June 14. It is a company disclosure, but it is the kind of deployment notice the contract asks for. e2 limits the effect to two models; it does not contradict a temporary slowdown.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post (with a typo), endorsed.

semantics.note: A firm 'will' forecast of a worldwide move toward sovereign AI and Chinese AI caused by the decision. The examples and the stated cause are kept, and no deadline is given.

contract.note: Reading 'rushing towards' as an actual shift in procurement or adoption, not just concern, is ordinary and fair. Requiring movement toward both sovereign and Chinese AI follows his words. Because there is no deadline, a short period without a shift cannot contradict the forecast.

evidence.note: October 1 ECB speech linking the June cut-off to European dependence and calling for domestic capability. It shows concern, not a measured shift in adoption. It is labelled a company disclosure, but it is an official speech.
September 16 Canada–Germany investment in sovereign AI. The cooperation predates the decision, the announcement does not tie it to the decision, and it shows no migration of customers.

reviews.rationale: There is no deadline and no conclusive event. The packet shows official concern and investment in sovereign AI, but no cross-country procurement or adoption evidence of a shift toward sovereign or Chinese AI caused by the decision. Nothing shows that such a shift failed to happen either.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post, endorsed.

semantics.note: 'Will have to' after 'no turning back' could be read as a prescription. But the next sentence, 'But they must', carries the normative part, so a forecast reading is defensible. It has no deadline and no defined scope.

contract.note: The contract reads it as government safety review plus actual blocking becoming established practice beyond the single June case. That is an ordinary reading. It rightly says one government acting identically everywhere is not required and that permanence cannot be shown in a finite period.

evidence.note: October 12 UK announcement of ongoing model evaluations by the AI Security Institute and stronger protections under consideration. It names no actual block of a deployment. It is labelled a company disclosure but is a government release.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. The only admitted evidence shows government evaluations, not any actual government block of a deployment on safety grounds after publication, so the early-resolution rule is not met. Nothing shows governments dropped the practice, so it is not contradicted.
